Persistent artifacts and review history

Source: vignettes/persistent-artifacts.Rmd
persistent-artifacts.Rmd

Saved work should remain verifiable after an R session ends. Graft keeps reports, tables, figures, and the exact evidence behind them as immutable revisions, then records explicit host review decisions so historical inspection stays separate from current reuse.

Save and reopen exact content

A local store keeps content-addressed files on disk and verifies digests on every read. Several R processes can write to one store: content writes use atomic staged renames, and per-stream advisory file locks serialize decision recording (on file systems that honor advisory locks). Saving bytes never approves them for reuse.

library(graft)
## 
## Attaching package: 'graft'
## The following object is masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     Recall
path <- tempfile("artifacts-")
store <- graft_store(path, create = TRUE)
original <- graft_save(
  store, "Original report", id = "report:daily", media_type = "text/plain"
)
corrected <- graft_save(
  store, "Corrected report", id = "report:daily", media_type = "text/plain"
)
reopened <- graft_store(path)
graft_read(reopened, original)@data
## [1] "Original report"
graft_read(reopened, corrected)@data
## [1] "Corrected report"
unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)

An ArtifactRef pairs a logical identity (@id) with an exact immutable revision (@revision). There is no mutable “latest” pointer: keep the references your workflow depends on, or record a decision stream when an application wants a reviewed current result.

Use graft_save_file() to ingest a bounded file from disk explicitly; strings passed to graft_save() are always treated as UTF-8 text content, never as file paths.

Pin evidence with selections

Declare dependencies by passing one ArtifactRef (or a list of them) to graft_save(). Calling graft_select() captures the roots together with their complete verified dependency closure as an immutable ArtifactSelection:

path <- tempfile("artifact-selection-")
store <- graft_store(path, create = TRUE)
vocabulary <- graft_save(
  store, '{"concept":"sample"}',
  id = "vocabulary:lab", media_type = "application/json"
)
dictionary <- graft_save(
  store, "name: assay", id = "dictionary:assay", media_type = "application/yaml",
  dependencies = vocabulary
)
report <- graft_save(
  store, "Assay interpretation", id = "report:assay", media_type = "text/plain",
  dependencies = dictionary
)
selection <- graft_select(store, report)
reopened_selection <- graft_read_selection(graft_store(path), selection@id)
reopened_selection@artifacts
## [[1]]
## <ArtifactRef report:assay@d2a512537a5aeb64afc0579652fe8fb59564e8dec59b3d590110c231b05588d4>
## 
## [[2]]
## <ArtifactRef dictionary:assay@514407a409fccc678ce634b5f7794a362960bc555acb66ee3928186e9c853a5f>
## 
## [[3]]
## <ArtifactRef vocabulary:lab@084f468d1dd656e8d360372e129b9421e28a561e4f26e48149a354868c14c6b9>
unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)

reopened_selection@artifacts contains the exact revisions of the report, dictionary, and vocabulary. max_artifacts bounds dependency traversal, store@max_bytes bounds aggregate selected payloads, and max_metadata_bytes / max_revision_bytes bound encoded metadata (1 MiB by default). Reading a selection re-verifies the entire dependency chain.

Record acceptance and withdrawal

Applications decide whether a candidate is acceptable and who may use it. Graft records each decision in a named decision stream. Supply the expected predecessor (expected = NULL for the first decision, or the prior Decision) and a stable request key so stale reviews fail and retries are idempotent:

path <- tempfile("artifact-decisions-")
store <- graft_store(path, create = TRUE)
report <- graft_save(
  store, "Reviewed report", id = "report", media_type = "text/plain"
)
accepted <- graft_accept(
  store, report, stream = "research:topic", key = "review-1", expected = NULL,
  actor = "reviewer:alice",
  reason = "Supporting evidence reviewed", purpose = "research"
)
input <- graft_recall(
  store, "research:topic", purpose = "research", eligible = TRUE
)
input@artifacts
## [[1]]
## <Artifact report@be41974429575fb1dffa3a66cc3e2cc4e3f3d6dd9983ef6cb558e8b3de05d147 media_type=text/plain bytes=15>
withdrawn <- graft_withdraw(
  store, "research:topic", expected = accepted, key = "withdraw-1",
  actor = "reviewer:alice", reason = "Evidence needs correction"
)
graft_history(store, "research:topic")[[1L]]@action
## [1] "accept"
graft_history(store, "research:topic")[[2L]]@action
## [1] "withdraw"
unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
  • eligible = TRUE stands in for your application’s current access check.
  • graft_recall() verifies eligibility, purpose match, the stream’s current accepted head, and every selected byte. After withdrawal it returns status "withdrawn" with no artifact payloads.
  • graft_history() and graft_read() keep earlier decisions and revisions inspectable for audit without re-approving them for reuse.
  • Decision@selection holds the exact selection digest so histories can be inspected without materializing payloads.

List what is kept

graft_streams() returns each stream’s current decision so an application can display what it has kept without maintaining a separate catalog. Pass purpose to filter by purpose, and inspect @action to distinguish accepted streams from withdrawn ones:

path <- tempfile("artifact-streams-")
store <- graft_store(path, create = TRUE)
report <- graft_save(store, "Reviewed report", id = "report")
graft_accept(
  store, report, stream = "project:reactor", key = "keep-1", expected = NULL,
  actor = "reviewer:alice", reason = "Kept to the project", purpose = "kept"
)
## <Decision accept stream=project:reactor sequence=1 id=7f8e25d1c66d60ead067f55450c776643232cc64a24f23e6e8863d27c36de404>
kept <- graft_streams(store, purpose = "kept")
vapply(kept, \(x) paste(x@stream, x@action), character(1))
## [1] "project:reactor accept"
unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)

Listing reads decision metadata only—it returns no artifact payloads and requires no eligibility callback. Streams are returned ordered by name.

Use PostgreSQL scopes

For multi-user or database-backed apps, graft_store_postgres() provides the exact same API inside a DBI transaction owned by your application:

DBI::dbWithTransaction(connection, {
  # Derive scope from authenticated identity and check access first.
  store <- graft_store_postgres(
    connection, scope = trusted_scope, create = TRUE
  )
  ref <- graft_save(store, "Accepted text", id = "note", media_type = "text/plain")
  accepted <- graft_accept(
    store, ref, stream = "note", key = "review-1", expected = NULL,
    actor = trusted_actor,
    reason = "Explicit review", purpose = "reader-context"
  )
  # Application catalog writes can commit atomically in the same transaction.
})

Every retained row in graft_artifact_objects belongs to one scope, and a transaction-level advisory lock serializes operations within that scope. Rolling back the transaction undoes every write cleanly. Because the scope key isolates data rather than authenticating callers, applications should always derive scope from authenticated identity and never let a model choose it.
